drhp.business: GNA Axles manufactures automotive transmission components — rear axle shafts, spindles and drive shafts — for Off-Highway (tractor), Commercial Vehicle and, increasingly, SUV applications. It supplies domestic and international OEMs from two integrated manufacturing facilities in Punjab, India, and is now diversifying into Light Vehicle, Passenger Vehicle and EV components through a new wholly owned subsidiary.

drhp.expansion: GNA Axles operates two manufacturing units in Punjab (Mehtiana, Hoshiarpur and Gulab Garh Jattan, Kapurthala). Historically, the Company built out a new forging shop and an SUV axle machining line (construction initiated 2017), opened a new machine shop for off-highway axle shafts (2018), initiated setting up of an SUV plant (2019) and commenced production at the SUV plant (2023); overall installed capacity was increased to 6.7 million components in 2021-22. risks.note: Exports to the USA were highly impacted by tariffs imposed by the US Government during FY2025-26, driving an overall drop of around 4% in total sales; management flags that any further increase or new imposition of US tariffs can adversely impact export revenues and demand for the Company's products in the US Commercial Vehicle market.
risks.risk: US tariff / trade-policy exposure on exports

risks.note: The Company's business is heavily dependent on demand from OEM customers (tractor and commercial vehicle manufacturers) in India and abroad; a slowdown among these customers directly affects the Company's volumes and top line.
risks.risk: Dependence on OEM customer demand, both domestic and export

risks.note: A material share of revenue comes from exports (North America, Europe and other overseas markets), exposing the Company to demand slowdowns, currency and trade-policy shifts in those specific geographies.

The Company operates in a single business segment (manufacturing automobile components), with no separate segment reporting; diversification into LV/PV/EV components via GNA Mobility Limited is only in its early, pre-operational stage.

Management notes escalating geopolitical tensions (including in West Asia), a fragile global economy entering CY2026, higher policy uncertainty, and volatile trade/tariff conditions as factors that could affect demand and the Company's operations.

Demand for the Company's core products is closely linked to factors such as monsoon performance, GST rates on tractors, and government infrastructure/agriculture spending, making revenue sensitive to these external and seasonal drivers.
risks.risk: Cyclicality tied to tractor and commercial vehicle demand drivers

risks.note: The Company relies on centralised sourcing and vendor management for raw material procurement, especially steel, indicating exposure to steel price and supply conditions.

This sits within the broader Indian automotive industry (2W/3W/PV/CV/off-highway), which grew from 21.6 million units (FY20) to 28.2 million units (FY26) at a 4.6% CAGR and is projected to reach 35-45 million units by FY31 (6-8% CAGR).
